sections.subtitle: Izaijino proroštvo: zastor koji prekriva sve narode
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar tumači Izaijin pokrivač kao tamni oblak smrti nad narodima
sections.content:
Nakon molitve krunice Vladimir Grebenar prelazi na tumačenje svete riječi. Čita odlomak iz **Knjige proroka Izaije**: Gospodin nad vojskama priredit će svim narodima na gori gozbu od pretiline, raskinut će zastor koji zastire sve narode i pokrivač koji pokriva sva plemena, uništit će smrt zauvijek, otrti suzu sa svakog lica i skinuti sramotu svoga naroda. Odlomak završava klicanjem: „Gle, ovo je Bog naš, u njega se uzdasmo, on nas je spasio.“

Grebenar to naziva važnim proroštvom. Ističe da poruka nije bila namijenjena samo izraelskom narodu osam stoljeća prije Krista. Kao zapisana i živa Božja riječ, kaže, odnosi se i na današnje vrijeme. Zato postavlja ključno pitanje: kakav je to pokrivač koji zastire sve narode?

Odgovor traži u duhovnoj sferi, u svijetu koji se ne vidi prirodnim očima, iako ga, prema njegovim riječima, neki imaju milost vidjeti. Govori o svojevrsnoj **duhovnoj kulisi ili scenografiji koja nije nimalo bezazlena**. Sveto pismo smatra duhovnom knjigom koja otkriva duhovnu stvarnost. Izaija je, tumači on, taj pokrivač doista vidio jer mu ga je Bog pokazao: riječ je o **tamnom oblaku smrti koji se nadvije nad neki prostor**.

Naglašava da prirodne okolnosti tu ništa ne govore. Dan može biti sunčan, oblaci svijetli ili nebo potpuno vedro, a da u duhovnom svijetu nad tim područjem ipak leži tamni prekrivač. Sunce izlazi i zalazi nad svim narodima kao prirodno svjetlo. Grebenar međutim drži da priroda i materija na skrovit način otkrivaju i poučavaju o onome što je duhovno. Dodaje da su do te spoznaje razumom došli još i antički filozofi.
sections.subtitle_en: Isaiah's prophecy: the veil that covers all peoples
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar interprets Isaiah's veil as a dark cloud of death over the nations
sections.content_en:
After praying the rosary, Vladimir Grebenar moves on to the interpretation of the Holy Word. He reads a passage from the **Book of the Prophet Isaiah**: on this mountain the Lord of hosts will make for all peoples a feast of rich food, He will destroy the veil that veils all peoples and the sheet that covers all nations, He will swallow up death forever, wipe away tears from every face, and remove the reproach of His people. The passage ends with acclaim: "Behold, this is our God; we have waited for Him, that He might save us."

Grebenar calls this an important prophecy. He emphasizes that the message was not intended only for the people of Israel eight centuries before Christ. As the written and living Word of God, he says, it applies to our time as well. Therefore, he poses the key question: what kind of veil is it that covers all peoples?

He seeks the answer in the spiritual sphere, in a world not seen with natural eyes, although, according to his words, some have the grace to see it. He speaks of a kind of **spiritual backdrop or scenery that is not at all harmless**. He considers Sacred Scripture to be a spiritual book that reveals spiritual reality. Isaiah, he interprets, truly saw that veil because God showed it to him: it is a matter of a **dark cloud of death that hangs over a space**.

He emphasizes that natural circumstances say nothing here. The day may be sunny, the clouds bright, or the sky completely clear, yet in the spiritual world a dark covering nevertheless lies over that area. The sun rises and sets over all peoples as natural light. Grebenar, however, holds that nature and matter in a hidden way reveal and teach about that which is spiritual. He adds that ancient philosophers had also arrived at that insight through reason.

sections.subtitle: Sunce kao slika Krista i dar slobodne volje
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o izboru između svjetla i tame
sections.content:
Grebenar se vraća slici koju, kako kaže, često ponavlja: **sunce je slika Božje svjetlosti, a ta svjetlost je Isus Krist**. Zato se Isusa naziva mladim suncem, kako stoji u Knjizi Otkrivenja. Iz iste slike tumači i Gospu „zaodjenutu u sunce“: ona je u svojoj utrobi nosila Isusa, koji je svjetlost. Podsjeća i na proslov Ivanova evanđelja: svjetlost je došla na svijet, ali su ljudi više voljeli tamu nego svjetlost jer su im djela bila zla.

Iz toga izvodi pouku o **slobodnoj volji**. Bog čovjeku daje slobodu da sam bira između svjetlosti i tame te kakva će djela činiti, a vjernik to mora prihvatiti. Ilustrira to iskustvom sa skupova koje vodi. Ljudi mu, osobito žene, često priđu i požale se da im je sin krenuo krivim putem, da kći živi s dečkom ili da se u obitelji događaju i gore stvari. Pitaju ga što da rade i kako da to prestane.

Njegov je odgovor dvojak. S jedne strane, treba moliti i postiti za dijete, supruga i druge ukućane. S druge strane, ako nakon nekog vremena nema promjene, treba prihvatiti da je riječ o izboru slobodne volje te osobe.
sections.subtitle_en: The sun as an image of Christ and the gift of free will
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host speaks about the choice between light and darkness
sections.content_en:
Grebenar returns to an image that, as he says, he often repeats: **the sun is an image of God's light, and that light is Jesus Christ**. That is why Jesus is called the dawn from on high / dayspring, as is found in the Book of Revelation. From the same image he also interprets Our Lady "clothed with the sun": she carried in her womb Jesus, who is the light. He also recalls the prologue of John's Gospel: the light came into the world, but people preferred darkness to light because their deeds were evil.

From this he draws a lesson about **free will**. God gives man the freedom to choose for himself between light and darkness and what deeds he will do, and the believer must accept this. He illustrates this with experience from gatherings he leads. People, especially women, often approach him and complain that their son has taken the wrong path, that their daughter is living with a boyfriend, or that even worse things are happening in the family. They ask him what to do and how to make it stop.

His answer is twofold. On the one hand, one must pray and fast for the child, spouse, and other household members. On the other hand, if after some time there is no change, one must accept that it is a choice of that person's free will.

sections.subtitle: Kada molitva oslobađa, a kada valja čekati
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar razlikuje porobljenu osobu koja se opire grijehu od one koja je izabrala zlo
sections.content:
Grebenar zatim razlikuje dvije vrste situacija. Prva je kada je čovjek **porobljen, ali to ne želi i opire se**. Kao primjer navodi dijete začeto u preljubu ili na neki drugi nedoličan način. Duh pod kojim je začeto, tumači on, prati to dijete i kada odraste. Osoba tada griješi pod silom jačom od sebe same, primjerice uđe u odnos u koji ne bi smjela ući. Kada za to saznaju otac, majka, brat ili sestra, mogu je **postom i molitvom osloboditi**. Uvjet je da se i sama osoba tome opire. Tada su, kaže, molitve plodonosne.

Druga je situacija kada je netko **svjesno odlučio tako živjeti, brani to i ustraje u tome**. Tada ga, po Grebenarovim riječima, nitko ne može promijeniti. Članu obitelji preostaje prikazivati ga na misama i u molitvama, biti strpljiv i čekati.

Zaključuje da ukućani, braća, sestre i ostali imaju slobodnu volju i mogu izabrati tamu umjesto svjetla, a Bog ih u tome neće spriječiti. Bog Otac neće ni jednom čovjeku oduzeti dar slobodne volje. Ističe i da se u raj ne može ući niti se spasiti onaj tko srcem ne ljubi Boga i ne radi za kraljevstvo Božje. **Kršćanstvo, poručuje, nije religija sile**, nego objavljena istina u koju se vjeruje srcem i slobodnom voljom, i po tome se razlikuje od drugih religija.
sections.subtitle_en: When prayer delivers, and when one must wait
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar distinguishes an enslaved person who resists sin from one who has chosen evil
sections.content_en:
Grebenar then distinguishes two types of situations. The first is when a person is **enslaved, but does not want it and resists**. As an example, he mentions a child conceived in adultery or in some other improper manner. The spirit under which they were conceived, he explains, accompanies that child even into adulthood. The person then sins under a power stronger than themselves, for instance entering into a relationship they should not enter. When the father, mother, brother, or sister learns of this, they can **deliver them through fasting and prayer**. The condition is that the person themselves also resists it. Then, he says, prayers are fruitful.

The other situation is when someone has **consciously decided to live that way, defends it, and perseveres in it**. Then, in Grebenar's words, no one can change them. What remains for the family member is to offer them up at Masses and in prayers, be patient, and wait.

He concludes that household members, brothers, sisters, and others have free will and can choose darkness instead of light, and God will not stop them from doing so. God the Father will not take away the gift of free will from any human being. He also points out that no one can enter heaven or be saved who does not love God with their heart and work for the kingdom of God. **Christianity, he conveys, is not a religion of force**, but a revealed truth believed in with the heart and free will, and in this it differs from other religions.

sections.subtitle: Obrezanje srca: bolan put unutarnjeg pročišćenja
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava zašto je obrezanje srca bolno
sections.content:
Grebenar spominje da je o istoj temi govorio i na jednom nedavnom skupu: **koliko boli obrezanje srca**. Obrezanje srca definira kao promjenu srca i nutrine. Tko je prošao proces unutarnjeg pročišćenja, kaže, zna koliko je on bolan.

Objašnjava zašto Stari zavjet za to uzima obredni primjer **tjelesnog obrezanja**. Židovski dječaci obrezivani su osmi dan, pa tako i Isus. Malo dijete ne može riječima izreći koliko ga boli, može samo zaplakati i od straha brzo zaspati. Odrasli koji su prošli taj zahvat svjedočili su da jako boli. Obilježja tog čina su, sažima Grebenar, **bol i krv**.

Podsjeća da sveti Pavao uči kako tjelesno obrezanje samo po sebi ništa ne znači, nego treba obrezati srce. U tome Grebenar vidi i drugu poruku: obrezanje srca jednako boli.
sections.subtitle_en: Circumcision of the heart: a painful path of interior purification
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host explains why circumcision of the heart is painful
sections.content_en:
Grebenar mentions that he spoke on the same topic at a recent gathering: **how much circumcision of the heart hurts**. He defines circumcision of the heart as a change of heart and inner self. Whoever has undergone the process of interior purification, he says, knows how painful it is.

He explains why the Old Testament takes the ritual example of **physical circumcision** for this. Jewish baby boys were circumcised on the eighth day, and so was Jesus. A small child cannot express in words how much it hurts; it can only cry and quickly fall asleep from fear. Adults who have undergone that procedure have testified that it hurts immensely. The hallmarks of that act, Grebenar summarizes, are **pain and blood**.

He recalls that Saint Paul teaches that physical circumcision in itself means nothing, but rather that the heart must be circumcised. In that, Grebenar sees another message as well: circumcision of the heart hurts just as much.

sections.subtitle: Post kao obrezanje iznutra: „Lagan sam kao ptica“
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar svjedoči o vlastitom iskustvu dugotrajnog posta
sections.content:
Kao praktičan primjer obrezanja srca Grebenar navodi upravo završeni post. Onaj tko posti, kaže, **razapinje svoje tijelo** i klanja se Isusu Kristu. Post boli i tjelesna je bol, ali donosi milost i plodove. Nabraja što ljudi koji poste doživljavaju:

- oslobađaju se grešnih navika i poroka,
- ozdravljaju,
- netko se u obitelji obrati,
- mijenjaju se životne okolnosti,
- postaju strpljiviji i radosniji.

Iznosi i osobno iskustvo. Kada dugotrajno posti, osjeća se **„lagan kao ptica“**: treba mu manje sna, tijelo mu je spremnije i poletniji je. Post ga, kaže, čisti i obrezuje iznutra. Što je pala ljudska narav više pobijeđena i „komprimirana“, to je više milosti u čovjeku i to snažnije djeluje Duh Sveti.

Odatle izvodi razliku između **ljudi duha i ljudi tijela**. Ljudi duha vole postiti jer im je tako duh slobodniji. Ljudi tijela ne mogu postiti jer misle samo na dobar obrok. Kada dođe post, kaže, „mazne ribu“ pa sami sebe lažu da poste. Mnogi, tvrdi, ne poste ni na Čistu srijedu i Veliki petak, dva dana koja propisuje Crkva.

Na pitanje zašto neki ne mogu postiti odgovara da ne žele vršiti volju Božju. Kada je čovjek zaokupljen pitanjem što je Božja volja, Bog mu pritječe u pomoć i tada „sve može u onome koji ga jača“, jer Bog ide s onima koji idu za njim.
sections.subtitle_en: Fasting as circumcision from within: “I am light as a bird”
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar testifies about his own experience of long-term fasting
sections.content_en:
As a practical example of circumcision of the heart, Grebenar cites the just-completed fast. Whoever fasts, he says, **crucifies their flesh** and adores Jesus Christ. Fasting hurts and is bodily pain, but it brings grace and fruits. He enumerates what people who fast experience:

- they are freed from sinful habits and vices,
- they are healed,
- someone in the family converts,
- life circumstances change,
- they become more patient and joyful.

He also shares a personal experience. When he fasts for a prolonged period, he feels **“light as a bird”**: he needs less sleep, his body is readier, and he is more spirited. Fasting, he says, cleanses and circumcises him from within. The more fallen human nature is conquered and "compressed", the more grace there is in man and the more powerfully the Holy Spirit acts.

From this he derives the distinction between **people of the spirit and people of the flesh**. People of the spirit love to fast because their spirit is freer that way. People of the flesh cannot fast because they only think about a good meal. When fasting comes, he says, they "snatch fish" and lie to themselves that they are fasting. Many, he asserts, do not even fast on Ash Wednesday and Good Friday, the two days prescribed by the Church.

To the question of why some cannot fast, he replies that they do not want to do God's will. When a person is preoccupied with what God's will is, God comes to their aid and then "they can do all things through Him who strengthens them", because God goes with those who follow Him.
keywords_en: people of the spirit and people of the flesh

sections.subtitle: Farizejska vjera i Božja zaštita na prvoj crti
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj govori o prepoznavanju duhovne tame
sections.content:
Suprotnost obrezanom srcu Grebenar vidi u **farizejskoj vjeri**: vjerovanju „tradicionalno“, kroz folklor, običaj i hrvatstvo. Takvi ljudi, kaže, lažu sami sebe da su vjernici, a ništa se ne događa. Vjera i Crkva postaju im tek sredstvo za umirivanje savjesti. Više ih zanimaju politika i svjetovnost, druže se sa svima i svakim, a to pokazuje da im srce nije obrezano.

Obrezano srce i pročišćena nutrina, tumači, omogućuju čovjeku da **vidi duhovnu tamu oko sebe**. Takav čovjek ne ide tamo gdje je tama, osim ako ga Bog ne šalje. Poziva se na psalam: „Da mi je dolinom smrti proći, zla se ne bojim.“ Postoje, kaže, i geografska područja na kojima je tama velika.

No upravo ondje gdje je tama najveća, Bog izlijeva još veću milost na one koji vrše njegovu volju. Isus se, naglašava Grebenar, **ne povlači s prve linije**. On želi razoriti i razotkriti djela tame, pa onoga tko ondje vrši Božju volju posebno štiti. Izaijin tekst o tami koja zastire narode tumači kao sliku **rata u nebu između anđela svjetla i anđela tame**, koji se bore za to kakvo će duhovno nebo biti nad ljudima.
sections.subtitle_en: Pharisaic faith and God's protection on the front line
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host speaks about recognizing spiritual darkness
sections.content_en:
Grebenar sees the opposite of a circumcised heart in **Pharisaic faith**: believing "traditionally", through folklore, custom, and Croathood. Such people, he says, lie to themselves that they are believers, yet nothing happens. Faith and the Church become merely a means to soothe their conscience. They are more interested in politics and worldliness, mingle with anyone and everyone, and that shows their heart is not circumcised.

A circumcised heart and a purified interior, he explains, enable a person to **see the spiritual darkness around them**. Such a person does not go where darkness is, unless God sends them. He refers to the psalm: "Though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I fear no evil." There are also, he says, geographical regions where darkness is great.

Yet precisely where darkness is greatest, God pours out even greater grace upon those who do His will. Jesus, Grebenar emphasizes, **does not retreat from the front line**. He wants to destroy and expose the deeds of darkness, so He especially protects whoever does God's will there. He interprets Isaiah's text about the darkness covering the nations as an image of the **war in heaven between angels of light and angels of darkness**, fighting over what kind of spiritual heaven will be over the people.

sections.subtitle: Obrezanje naroda: Europa, pobačaj i prosvjedi u Francuskoj
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar govori o Europi koja više voli pobačaj od života
sections.content:
Iz osobne razine Grebenar prelazi na zajedničku: **kao što pojedinac treba obrezati srce, mora se dogoditi i obrezanje naroda**, a ono je uvijek bolno. Do toga dolazi, objašnjava, kada narod zastrani, odnosno kada većina pojedinaca u njemu više ljubi zlo i grijeh.

Kao primjer navodi narode nekad kršćanske Europe. Oni, kaže, više vole pobačaj nego život i više im je stalo do prava na ubojstvo djeteta nego do njegova rođenja. Posebno izdvaja Francusku, gdje je predsjednik Macron zatražio da se pravo na pobačaj unese u ustav. To naziva djelom bolesnih umova, a francuskog predsjednika oštro uspoređuje s „Hitlerom i Herodom ovog vremena“.

Osvrće se zatim na **prosvjede u Francuskoj i Belgiji**. Strani komentatori i analitičari, kaže, pitaju tko stoji iza njih i ne znaju odgovoriti. Grebenar odgovara da iza toga stoji sam Sotona i da nije potrebna nikakva organizacija. Opisuje što vidi na ulicama:

- mladi Francuzi izlaze zajedno s djecom migranata,
- nema francuskih zastava, nose se palestinske,
- nije jasno zašto prosvjeduju, navodno za bolje školstvo,
- mete su trgovine, obrti, OPG-ovi, mikropoduzeća i obiteljske radnje koje razaraju.

Razlog tome vidi u **duhu komunizma i socijalizma**, koji po njegovu tumačenju ide zajedno s duhom islama. Kao primjer navodi Bosnu i Hercegovinu, gdje, kaže, Bošnjaci jako žale za socijalizmom i tim vremenima.
sections.subtitle_en: Circumcision of the nation: Europe, abortion, and protests in France
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar speaks about Europe loving abortion more than life
sections.content_en:
From the personal level, Grebenar moves to the collective: **just as an individual needs to circumcise their heart, the circumcision of a nation must also take place**, and it is always painful. This occurs, he explains, when a nation goes astray, namely when the majority of individuals in it love evil and sin more.

As an example, he mentions the nations of once Christian Europe. They, he says, love abortion more than life and care more about the right to kill a child than about its birth. He singles out France in particular, where President Macron demanded that the right to abortion be enshrined in the constitution. He calls that the work of sick minds, and harshly compares the French president to "the Hitler and Herod of our time".

He then reflects on the **protests in France and Belgium**. Foreign commentators and analysts, he says, ask who is behind them and cannot answer. Grebenar answers that behind it stands Satan himself and that no organization is needed. He describes what he sees on the streets:

- young French people go out together with children of migrants,
- there are no French flags, Palestinian ones are carried,
- it is not clear why they are protesting, ostensibly for better education,
- the targets are shops, trade crafts, family farms (OPGs), micro-enterprises, and family workshops, which they destroy.

He sees the reason for this in the **spirit of communism and socialism**, which in his interpretation goes hand in hand with the spirit of Islam. As an example, he cites Bosnia and Herzegovina, where, he says, Bosniaks deeply grieve for socialism and those times.

sections.subtitle: Generacija Z: odgojena da ne preuzima odgovornost
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj kritizira školski odgoj mladih generacija
sections.content:
Zašto su privatne trgovine i poduzeća postali meta europske mladeži? Grebenar odgovara da je Europa odgojila **generaciju Z** tako da prihvati komunizam, odnosno da bude **nesposobna preuzeti odgovornost** za sebe, svoju obitelj i domovinu.

Krivnju pripisuje školskom sustavu. Djecu se, kaže, uči da su homoseksualizam, koji naziva sodomijom, i pobačaj nešto dobro, a u to vjeruju i mnogi mladi učitelji, „gotovo opsjednuti“ time. Tvrdi da mnogi od njih imaju raspadnute brakove ili ne zasnivaju obitelj, a neki nakon takvih predbračnih života ne mogu imati djece. Za sebe kaže da govori o nečemu što zna. Dodaje da toga možda manje ima u Hercegovini, ali u Hrvatskoj itekako. Roditelji pritom nisu svjesni što se događa, a dijete više vremena provede u školi nego kod kuće.

Posljedicu sažima pitanjem: ako mlada osoba nije sposobna preuzeti odgovornost za vlastitu budućnost, kako će preuzeti odgovornost za budućnost naroda? Takvi mladi traže da im **država riješi probleme**, a malo tko se pita koja je njegova vlastita uloga u društvu.

Poruku upućuje i francuskim prosvjednicima, među kojima su mladi, učitelji i sindikati: Macrona i njegovu vladu sami su birali. Francuski kršćani i katolici šutjeli su, kaže, dok je vlada odobravala pobačaj, istospolne zajednice i migrantsku politiku, a isto se, tvrdi, događa i u Hrvatskoj. Kada katolici šute, sustav im odgaja djecu. Takav duh, koji ne podnosi poduzetništvo ni obiteljski posao, naziva **duhom socijalizma i duhom antikrista**.
sections.subtitle_en: Generation Z: raised not to take responsibility
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host criticizes the school education of young generations
sections.content_en:
Why have private stores and businesses become the target of European youth? Grebenar answers that Europe has raised **Generation Z** to embrace communism, that is, to be **incapable of taking responsibility** for themselves, their families, and their homeland.

He places the blame on the school system. Children, he says, are taught that homosexuality, which he calls sodomy, and abortion are something good, and many young teachers, "almost obsessed" with it, believe this as well. He claims that many of them have broken marriages or do not start families, and some, after such premarital lifestyles, cannot have children. Regarding himself, he says he speaks of something he knows. He adds that there may be less of this in Hercegovina, but in Croatia very much so. Parents, meanwhile, are not aware of what is happening, and a child spends more time at school than at home.

He summarizes the consequence with a question: if a young person is not capable of taking responsibility for their own future, how will they take responsibility for the future of the nation? Such young people demand that **the state solve their problems**, and hardly anyone asks what their own role in society is.

He also directs a message to the French protesters, including youth, teachers, and unions: they elected Macron and his government themselves. French Christians and Catholics remained silent, he says, while the government approved abortion, same-sex civil unions, and migrant policy, and the same, he claims, is happening in Croatia. When Catholics remain silent, the system raises their children. Such a spirit, which cannot stand entrepreneurship or family business, he calls the **spirit of socialism and the spirit of the antichrist**.

sections.subtitle: Povratak komunizma: od faraonova Egipta do Isusa tesara
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar uspoređuje komunizam s egipatskim ropstvom Izraelaca
sections.content:
Grebenar povezuje te pojave s Izaijinim pokrivačem. Danas je, kaže, u Europi i zapadnom svijetu na djelu **povratak komunizma**, tamnog prekrivača koji je nekad pokrivao istočni blok iza željezne zavjese. Oni njegovih godina i stariji, dodaje, toga se dobro sjećaju.

Komunizam definira kao stanje u kojem **država odlučuje što će čovjek raditi**. Prvu komunističku, socijalističku ekonomiju pronalazi u **Egiptu**: Izraelci su bili radnici, a Egipćani „članovi partije“ faraonova naroda. Faraon je imao jednu jedinu stranku i svi su radili za njega. Današnji povratak komunizma vidi kao sofisticiraniji i učinkovitiji od onoga nekad. U pozivima na prosvjede u Hrvatskoj u ime marksizma vidi djelo samog Sotone: mlade se poziva da mrze poduzetništvo i neovisnost te da država sve uzme i jednako raspodijeli.

Takvoj „socijalnoj pravdi“ suprotstavlja **Isusove kriterije**: „Komu je dano, njemu će se dati još više da obiluje, a tko misli da nešto ima, oduzet će mu se.“ Tumači da će Isus dati sve potrebno, i materijalno, onome tko širi kraljevstvo Božje.

Posebno naglašava da je **Krist bio poduzetan**. Trideset godina bio je tesar koji je svojim rukama stvarao, najprije uz svetog Josipa, a nakon Josipove smrti i sam. Isus i Josip imali su svoj posao, bili su neovisni i poduzetni. Grebenar dodaje da nije problem raditi kod drugoga, ali takvi poslovi čekaju one kojima su namijenjeni.
sections.subtitle_en: The return of communism: from Pharaoh's Egypt to Jesus the carpenter
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar compares communism to the Egyptian slavery of the Israelites
sections.content_en:
Grebenar connects these phenomena with Isaiah's veil. Today, he says, in Europe and the Western world, a **return of communism** is at work, a dark covering that once covered the Eastern Bloc behind the Iron Curtain. Those of his age and older, he adds, remember it well.

He defines communism as a state in which **the state decides what a person will do**. He finds the first communist, socialist economy in **Egypt**: the Israelites were workers, and the Egyptians were "party members" of Pharaoh's people. Pharaoh had one single party and everyone worked for him. He views today's return of communism as more sophisticated and effective than the one in the past. In calls for protests in Croatia in the name of Marxism, he sees the work of Satan himself: young people are called upon to hate entrepreneurship and independence and to demand that the state take everything and distribute it equally.

To such "social justice" he contrasts **Jesus' criteria**: "To everyone who has, more will be given and he will have an abundance; but from him who has not, even what he has will be taken away." He explains that Jesus will provide everything necessary, including material things, to whoever spreads the Kingdom of God.

He particularly emphasizes that **Christ was enterprising**. For thirty years He was a carpenter who created with His hands, first alongside Saint Joseph, and after Joseph's death on His own. Jesus and Joseph had their own business, they were independent and enterprising. Grebenar adds that there is no problem working for someone else, but such jobs await those for whom they are intended.

sections.subtitle: Molitva i post samo su jedna strana kovanice
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj poziva obitelji da pokrenu vlastiti posao
sections.content:
Iz primjera Isusa tesara Grebenar izvodi konkretan poziv hrvatskom narodu: **neka mnogo obitelji pokrene vlastiti posao**, obrt, OPG ili mikropoduzeće. Ništa, kaže, nije takav lijek društvu kao malo poduzetništvo koje izrasta iz obitelji. Kada otac i majka rade zajedno, i djeca će sutra tako raditi. Neće, slikovito kaže, „vući načelnika i župana za ruku“ da im zaposle dijete, nego će stvarati vlastitim rukama.

Naglašava da **molitva i post nisu dovoljni**. Uspoređuje ih s kovanicom koja ima pismo i glavu: molitva i post samo su jedna njezina strana. Druga je strana pokretanje inicijativa. Tko nema vlastitu tvrtku, neka bude poduzetan ondje gdje radi, u privatnom ili javnom poduzeću, i pokrene nešto novo.

I time se, poručuje, **razaraju djela tame**. Takav čovjek neće samo kritizirati državu i politiku. Kada sam nešto pokreće, prepoznat će i koga treba birati na izborima, jer će vidjeti koji su ljudi oni koje Bog šalje.
sections.subtitle_en: Prayer and fasting are only one side of the coin
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host calls on families to start their own businesses
sections.content_en:
From the example of Jesus the carpenter, Grebenar draws a concrete appeal to the Croatian people: **let many families start their own business**, craft, family farm (OPG), or micro-enterprise. Nothing, he says, is such a remedy for society as small entrepreneurship that grows out of the family. When father and mother work together, the children will also work that way tomorrow. They will not, as he puts it colorfully, "drag the municipal mayor and county prefect by the arm" to get their child employed, but will create with their own hands.

He emphasizes that **prayer and fasting are not enough**. He compares them to a coin that has heads and tails: prayer and fasting are only one of its sides. The other side is taking initiatives. Whoever does not have their own company should be enterprising where they work, in a private or public company, and initiate something new.

And by this, he conveys, **the works of darkness are destroyed**. Such a person will not merely criticize the state and politics. When they initiate something themselves, they will also recognize whom to vote for in elections, because they will see which people are those whom God sends.

sections.subtitle: Kad narod zastrani: Irska, demokracija i opomena iz Akite
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar navodi irske referendume kao primjer zastranjenja naroda
sections.content:
„Narod može oboljeti“, upozorava Grebenar i tvrdi da **demokracija nije temeljna vrijednost onako kako je Bog vidi**. Kao primjer navodi **Irsku**: irski narod je na dva referenduma izglasao najprije pravo na pobačaj, a zatim pravo istospolnih parova na posvajanje djece. Podsjeća da su se katolici prije dvadesetak godina dičili „katoličkom Irskom“, a ona je, kaže, sama donijela „sotonine zakone“.

Sveto pismo, osobito Stari zavjet, uči da cijeli narod ili njegov veći dio može krenuti krivim smjerom. Kada većina prezre ono što je Božje, Bog dopušta nešto bolno kako bi **obrezao narod**. Usporedbu povlači s pojedincem: tko se ne ponizi pred Bogom postom i sam ne razapne svoje tijelo, toga će Bog poniziti na svoj način kako bi ga popravio.

Ako se narod klanja đavlu i bira ga umjesto Oca nebeskoga, Bog to po Grebenarovu tumačenju pravedno dopušta: onaj kojemu se narod klanja počinje vladati njime. Među takve idole ubraja i **nacionalizam**, pretjeranu ljubav prema zastavi, hrvatstvu, srpstvu ili amerikanizmu, kao u Njemačkoj za vrijeme Hitlera. Đavao, kaže, ne zna vladati nego samo udarati. Tada stradaju i nevini i prolijeva se nevina krv.

Podsjeća na poruku iz **Akite**: ako se čovječanstvo ne obrati, doći će kazna gora od potopa, a stradat će i nedužni, mnogi svećenici i dobri vjernici. To su, zaključuje, duhovni zakoni. Zato su vjernici dužni opominjati sugrađane da se ne poigravaju s Bogom jer je krajnje vrijeme za obraćenje. Dio završava molitvom: „Bože, spasi nas od onoga što dolazi.“
sections.subtitle_en: When a nation goes astray: Ireland, democracy, and the warning from Akita
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar cites Irish referendums as an example of a nation going astray
sections.content_en:
“A nation can fall ill”, warns Grebenar, and asserts that **democracy is not a fundamental value the way God sees it**. As an example, he mentions **Ireland**: the Irish people voted in two referendums first for the right to abortion, and then for the right of same-sex couples to adopt children. He recalls that twenty years ago Catholics took pride in "Catholic Ireland", yet it, he says, enacted "Satan's laws" on its own.

Sacred Scripture, especially the Old Testament, teaches that an entire nation or the greater part of it can take the wrong direction. When the majority scorns what is God's, God allows something painful in order to **circumcise the nation**. He draws a comparison with the individual: whoever does not humble themselves before God through fasting and does not crucify their own flesh, God will humble in His own way in order to mend them.

If a nation bows down to the devil and chooses him instead of the heavenly Father, God, in Grebenar's interpretation, justly allows it: the one whom the nation worships begins to rule over it. Among such idols he also includes **nationalism**, excessive love toward the flag, Croathood, Serbhood, or Americanism, as in Germany during Hitler's time. The devil, he says, does not know how to rule, only how to strike. Then the innocent also suffer and innocent blood is shed.

He recalls the message from **Akita**: if humanity does not convert, a chastisement worse than the deluge will come, and the innocent, many priests, and good faithful will also perish. Those are, he concludes, spiritual laws. Therefore, the faithful have a duty to admonish their fellow citizens not to play games with God because it is the eleventh hour for conversion. The segment ends with a prayer: "God, save us from what is coming."

sections.subtitle: Nakon posta: odmor s Isusom, a ne od Isusa
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava kako ustrajati nakon završetka 40-dnevnog posta
sections.content:
Nakon psalma „Spomeni se, Gospodine, svoje ljubavi“ Grebenar čita odlomak iz **Poslanice Rimljanima**. Svi koje vodi Duh Božji sinovi su Božji. Primili su duha posinstva u kojem kliču „Aba, Oče“. Patnje sadašnjeg vremena ništa su prema budućoj slavi, a **sve stvorenje uzdiše i muči se u porođajnim bolima** do sada.

Tumači da riječi svetog Pavla o „svem stvorenju“ znače da uzdiše svaki pojedinac. Primjenjuje ih na upravo završeni četrdesetodnevni post. Oni koji su postili osjećaju se dobro, „lagani kao ptice“, mnogi su obiteljski problemi riješeni, mirniji su i Isus im je bliži. Ali neka ne poste deset ili petnaest dana, upozorava, pa će vidjeti kako se sve vraća.

Vjernik ne može ne postiti, ne ići na misu i ne moliti. Svaki je dan, kaže, utakmica i bitka za spasenje. Dopušta da se treba znati zaustaviti i odmoriti od posta, ali **i odmor mora biti molitva**. Ne smije se Isusu reći: „Sad je završio post, ćao, idem svojim putem na petnaest dana odmora od tebe.“ Tko tako govori, kaže, već je zgriješio i đavao dolazi odmah.

Nudi i ispravnu molitvu: „Isuse, završila sam s postom. Sad me ti odmori, pripremi me za nove zadaće, daj mi milost da uživam u tvojoj prisutnosti.“ Od Isusa se, poručuje, nije moguće i nije dopušteno odvojiti. Uzdišu i obitelji, jer danas nije jednostavno odgajati djecu, a uzdišu i narod i cijela Crkva.
sections.subtitle_en: After the fast: rest with Jesus, not from Jesus
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host explains how to persevere after the end of the 40-day fast
sections.content_en:
After the psalm "Remember, Lord, Your love", Grebenar reads a passage from the **Epistle to the Romans**. All who are led by the Spirit of God are sons of God. They have received the spirit of adoption in which they cry out, "Abba, Father". The sufferings of the present time are nothing compared to the future glory, and **all creation has been groaning and travailing in labor pains** until now.

He interprets Saint Paul's words about "all creation" to mean that every individual groans. He applies them to the just-concluded forty-day fast. Those who fasted feel good, "light as birds", many family problems have been resolved, they are calmer, and Jesus is closer to them. But let them not fast for ten or fifteen days, he warns, and they will see how everything returns.

A believer cannot fail to fast, fail to go to Mass, and fail to pray. Every day, he says, is a match and a battle for salvation. He grants that one must know how to pause and take a rest from fasting, but **rest too must be prayer**. One must not say to Jesus: "Now the fast has ended, bye, I'm going my own way for fifteen days of rest from You." Whoever speaks like that, he says, has already sinned and the devil comes immediately.

He also offers the proper prayer: "Jesus, I have finished fasting. Now You rest me, prepare me for new tasks, give me the grace to enjoy Your presence." From Jesus, he conveys, it is not possible and not permissible to separate oneself. Families groan too, because today it is not easy to raise children, and both the nation and the whole Church groan.

sections.subtitle: Porođajna bol i majčinstvo kao slika pročišćenja
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar opisuje majčinsku žrtvu i besane noći uz bolesno dijete
sections.content:
„Nema spasenja, nema vječnosti bez prolaska kroz porođajne boli“, kaže Grebenar. Uz tjelesno obrezanje uvodi još jednu sliku bolnog obrezanja srca: **porođajnu bol**. Žene znaju koliko porođaj boli, a ta bol je, tumači, slika ljudskog pročišćenja.

Trpljenje porođaja ženu priprema da se može predati djetetu. Nakon toga dolazi nova bol, koju u ljubavi podnosi za dijete. Opisuje je vrlo konkretno: dijete se budi noću, treba ga dojiti, dobije temperaturu, majka bdije noć i dan, pa se dogodi da u pet dana ukupno odspava deset sati. Tko ima djecu, kaže, zna što je to, a tko nema, teško može razumjeti. Još je teže kad istekne porodiljni dopust pa treba ići na posao, a dijete je bolesno i nema ga se kome ostaviti. Ako ide u vrtić, može se očekivati da će ondje opet dobiti temperaturu, i tako u krug.

Kako se ipak ide naprijed? **Kršćani se ne boje**, kaže Grebenar, nego idu u susret problemu i izazovu i gledaju naprijed. Tko gleda samo koliko će biti teško roditi i odgojiti dijete, taj neće dijete jer više voli sebe. Navodi i oca koji kaže „dosta je jedno, i jedno je previše“. Takve roditelje, smatra, ne vodi obrezano srce. Obrezanje srca znači predanje: **više ne živiš sebi, nego za drugoga**.
sections.subtitle_en: Labor pain and motherhood as an image of purification
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar describes maternal sacrifice and sleepless nights with a sick child
sections.content_en:
“There is no salvation, there is no eternity without passing through labor pains”, says Grebenar. Alongside physical circumcision, he introduces another image of painful circumcision of the heart: **labor pain**. Women know how much childbirth hurts, and that pain is, he interprets, an image of human purification.

The suffering of childbirth prepares a woman to be able to surrender herself to the child. After that comes a new pain, which she bears in love for the child. He describes it very concretely: the child wakes at night, needs breastfeeding, gets a fever, the mother keeps vigil night and day, so it happens that in five days she sleeps a total of ten hours. Whoever has children, he says, knows what that is, and whoever does not can hardly understand. It is even harder when maternity leave expires and one must go to work, while the child is sick and there is no one to leave it with. If the child goes to kindergarten, it can be expected that it will get a fever there again, and so in a loop.

How does one nevertheless move forward? **Christians are not afraid**, says Grebenar, but go out to meet the problem and challenge and look forward. Whoever looks only at how difficult it will be to give birth and raise a child does not want a child because they love themselves more. He also mentions a father who says "one is enough, and one is too much". Such parents, he considers, are not led by a circumcised heart. Circumcision of the heart means surrender: **you no longer live for yourself, but for another**.

sections.subtitle: Svjedočanstvo: odricanje od košarke radi obitelji
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar svjedoči kako je u 26. godini prekinuo s košarkom
sections.content:
Da se mnogočega treba odreći, Grebenar potkrepljuje vlastitim iskustvom. Igrao je **profesionalnu košarku** i trenirao dvaput dnevno. Kasnije je prešao u drugu ligu, „poluprofesionalno, poluamaterski“, s jednim treningom dnevno. Kada mu se rodilo prvo dijete, sve se promijenilo.

Shvatio je da mu je košarka postala konkurencija vremenu s djetetom i pomoći u obitelji, gdje je najveći teret nosila supruga. Zato je **s 26 godina prestao igrati**. Odlučio je da je za obitelj korisnije to vrijeme uložiti u nastavak školovanja. Potom su došli drugo i treće dijete. Otprilike pet godina nije išao ni na košarku ni na nogomet, iako ih silno voli i s loptom je od djetinjstva, „u krvi, u nogama i u srcu“. Djecu su supruga i on podizali sami, oboje su radili, a kod kuće su ga čekali djeca i supruga.

Sjeća se koliko je bio sretan kada je nakon pet godina prvi put opet zaigrao nogomet. Kaže da mu nije bilo žao i da se tim iskustvom, ako smije reći, ponosi. Zahvaljuje Bogu što ga je kroz tih pet godina **očistio od navezanosti** i dao mu nešto važnije. Poslije mu je igra bila još draža: mogao je igrati i zabaviti se, ali nije morao i ništa mu nije nedostajalo. Završava riječima svetog Pavla: „Sve mogu u onome koji me jača.“
sections.subtitle_en: Testimony: giving up basketball for the sake of the family
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar testifies how at age 26 he stopped playing basketball
sections.content_en:
That many things must be renounced Grebenar substantiates with his own experience. He played **professional basketball** and trained twice a day. Later he moved to the second league, "semi-professionally, semi-amateurly", with one training session a day. When his first child was born, everything changed.

He realized that basketball had become competition for time with the child and helping out in the family, where his wife bore the greatest burden. Therefore, **at age 26 he stopped playing**. He decided it was more beneficial for the family to invest that time in continuing his education. Then came the second and third children. For about five years he did not play basketball or soccer, although he loves them immensely and has been with a ball since childhood, "in the blood, in the legs, and in the heart". His wife and he raised the children by themselves, both worked, and at home his children and wife awaited him.

He remembers how happy he was when, after five years, he played soccer again for the first time. He says he did not regret it and that he is proud of that experience, if he may say so. He thanks God that over those five years He **cleansed him of attachment** and gave him something more important. Later, playing was even sweeter to him: he could play and have fun, but he did not have to, and he lacked nothing. He concludes with the words of Saint Paul: "I can do all things through Him who strengthens me."

sections.subtitle: Između progresivaca i nacionalista: Crkva kao treći put
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj tumači Gospinu poruku od 25. listopada
sections.content:
Iz osobnih navezanosti Grebenar prelazi na **navezanosti naroda** i upozorava da se ne griješi ni osobnim grijesima ni grijesima naroda. Narodi svijeta danas su, kaže, podijeljeni u **dva tabora**.

Prvi je ljevičarski, liberalan i „progresivan“, ali njegov progres vodi, tvrdi, „prema dolje, u smrt, u pakao“, a ne prema nebu i slobodi. U Hrvatskoj su to po njegovim riječima oni koji se predstavljaju kao antifašisti. Drugi tabor je **nacionalizam**, zaljubljenost u vlastitu naciju, koji također vodi u pakao. Oba tabora danas istodobno rastu i, prema Grebenaru, dolaze od istog duha, **duha antikrista**.

Kao odgovor ističe rast **Crkve**, „nešto treće“ što Bog daje. Poziva se na Gospinu poruku od **25. listopada** i kaže da je treba dobro pročitati. Mržnja i rat šire se ljudskim srcima jer ljudi gledaju svoje sebične interese, a Bog im želi dati mir koji oni ne žele. Grebenar dodaje da mnogi koji idu u crkvu i nazivaju se Hrvatima i katolicima ne žele mir, jer **duh nacionalizma, kad jača, priprema narod za rat**.

Zato poziva hrvatske katolike da se ne ujedinjuju na ideji hrvatstva, nego **oko križa**. Križ, ističe, nije ideja nego poziv. Ako križ nije na prvom mjestu i u središtu ujedinjenja, „neće biti dobro“. Progresivci križ preziru, a nacionalisti ga koriste kao sredstvo za ostvarenje nacionalnih interesa i rješavanje „hrvatskog pitanja“. To pitanje i podjele u društvu može riješiti samo Krist Gospodin, ali tek ako ga ljudi stave na prvo mjesto, jer je za njih umro na križu.
sections.subtitle_en: Between progressives and nationalists: the Church as a third path
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host interprets Our Lady's message of October 25
sections.content_en:
From personal attachments, Grebenar moves to the **attachments of nations** and warns against sinning either through personal sins or the sins of a nation. The nations of the world today are, he says, divided into **two camps**.

The first is leftist, liberal, and "progressive", but its progress leads, he asserts, "downward, into death, into hell", and not toward heaven and freedom. In Croatia, according to his words, these are those who present themselves as anti-fascists. The second camp is **nationalism**, falling in love with one's own nation, which likewise leads to hell. Both camps are growing simultaneously today and, according to Grebenar, come from the same spirit, the **spirit of the antichrist**.

As a response, he points to the growth of the **Church**, "something third" that God provides. He refers to Our Lady's message of **October 25** and says it must be read carefully. Hatred and war are spreading through human hearts because people look to their selfish interests, while God wants to give them peace that they do not want. Grebenar adds that many who go to church and call themselves Croats and Catholics do not want peace, because **the spirit of nationalism, as it grows stronger, prepares a nation for war**.

He therefore calls on Croatian Catholics not to unite on the idea of Croathood, but **around the cross**. The cross, he emphasizes, is not an idea but a calling. If the cross is not in the first place and at the center of unification, "it will not be good". Progressives despise the cross, while nationalists use it as a tool to achieve national interests and resolve the "Croatian question". That question and the divisions in society can be resolved only by Christ the Lord, but only if people put Him first, because He died on the cross for them.

sections.subtitle: Kritika ujedinjenja desnice bez Krista
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar upozorava na opasnost ujedinjenja desnice koje nije utemeljeno na Kristu
sections.content:
Grebenar izravno kritizira dio hrvatske političke scene. Problem je, kaže, kada pojedine **desne političke stranke ne vjeruju u Isusa svim srcem**, nego u svoje fotelje i utjecaj, na drugoj strani vide neprijatelje, a križ i Crkva im služe za vlastite ideje. To, upozorava, vodi u propast cijelog naroda i tu opasnost treba spriječiti.

Odbacuje svako ujedinjenje desnice koje se ne temelji na križu, Svetom pismu i Božjoj riječi, nego samo na rušenju komunizma i antifašizma. Takvo **„ujedinjenje desnice“, kaže, zapravo i ne postoji**. Umjesto toga treba rasti zajednica onih koji su Kristovi, u hrvatskom narodu i u narodima svijeta. To su ljudi koji vjeruju u Isusa, mole i poste, ali čine i nešto više od toga.

Kada križ bude temeljna vrijednost, Bog će, poručuje, učiniti sve za što vjernici mole, ukloniti nepravdu te razoriti sotonska djela i lažne utvrde u Hrvatskoj, kako on kaže, antifašizma i komunizma.
sections.subtitle_en: Criticism of unifying the right without Christ
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar warns of the danger of unifying the right that is not founded on Christ
sections.content_en:
Grebenar directly criticizes part of the Croatian political scene. The problem is, he says, when individual **right-wing political parties do not believe in Jesus with all their heart**, but in their armchairs and influence, see enemies on the other side, and the cross and the Church serve them for their own ideas. That, he warns, leads to the ruin of the entire nation, and that danger must be prevented.

He rejects any unification of the right that is not based on the cross, Sacred Scripture, and the Word of God, but merely on the tearing down of communism and anti-fascism. Such **“unification of the right”, he says, does not actually exist**. Instead, the community of those who belong to Christ must grow, within the Croatian nation and among the nations of the world. These are people who believe in Jesus, pray, and fast, but also do something more than that.

When the cross becomes the fundamental value, God will, he conveys, do everything the faithful pray for, remove injustice, and tear down Satan's works and false strongholds in Croatia, as he says, of anti-fascism and communism.

sections.subtitle: Plodovi posta: zgrada Vjesnika i kosti žrtava iz Slovenije
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj povezuje post s povratkom posmrtnih ostataka žrtava iz 1945.
sections.content:
Kao konkretne plodove Grebenar navodi događaje koje povezuje s postom. Zajednica je **40 dana postila i molila** da se razotkriju laži „komunističkih medija“ o žrtvama Drugog svjetskog rata, a nakon toga je, kaže, izgorjela zgrada **Vjesnika**. Takve se bitke, ističe, vode Božjom riječju, a ne političkim idejama, jer je riječ o duhovnom pokrivaču o kojem govori prorok Izaija.

Drugi primjer je **povratak kostiju iz Slovenije**, posmrtnih ostataka hrvatskih vojnika i civila ubijenih u svibnju 1945. godine. Prema njegovim riječima, to se dogodilo nakon 85 godina i tek kada su tisuće ljudi postile na tu nakanu. Hrvatski nadbiskup ih je pokopao katoličkim obredom, dostojanstveno. Grebenar pita koliki je prekrivač smrti nad Hrvatskom i Slovenijom kada desetljećima nije bilo moguće vratiti kosti ubijenih i dostojno ih pokopati.

Prenosi i riječi jednog bivšeg hrvatskog ministra zdravstva: kad god bi se nešto pokušalo, čak i uz pristanak ljevice, uvijek bi se nešto ispriječilo, što je ministar nazvao nevjerojatnim. Grebenar to tumači kao djelovanje **duhova smrti**, velikog tamnog oblaka koji priječi. Kada se ciljano posti i moli protiv toga, Bog, kaže, razara te utvrde.

Zgradu Vjesnika opisuje kao zgradu koju je osnovala Komunistička partija Hrvatske „da piše laži i sakrije istinu“. U njoj su, tvrdi, bila dva kata Udbe koja su nadzirala informacije koje izlaze van. „To su Božji ratovi, to su Božje bitke“, zaključuje.
sections.subtitle_en: Fruits of fasting: the Vjesnik building and bones of victims from Slovenia
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host connects fasting with the return of mortal remains of victims from 1945
sections.content_en:
As concrete fruits, Grebenar cites events that he connects with fasting. The community **fasted and prayed for 40 days** that the lies of the "communist media" about the victims of World War II be exposed, and after that, he says, the **Vjesnik** building burned down. Such battles, he points out, are fought with God's word and not with political ideas, because it is a matter of the spiritual veil spoken of by the prophet Isaiah.

The second example is the **return of bones from Slovenia**, the mortal remains of Croatian soldiers and civilians killed in May 1945. According to his words, that happened after 85 years and only when thousands of people fasted for that intention. A Croatian archbishop buried them with a Catholic rite, with dignity. Grebenar asks how great the covering of death over Croatia and Slovenia must be when for decades it was impossible to return the bones of the slain and bury them with dignity.

He also conveys the words of a former Croatian minister of health: whenever something was attempted, even with the consent of the left, something would always stand in the way, which the minister called unbelievable. Grebenar interprets this as the working of **spirits of death**, a great dark cloud that obstructs. When targeted fasting and prayer are made against it, God, he says, destroys those strongholds.

He describes the Vjesnik building as a building founded by the Communist Party of Croatia "to write lies and hide the truth". In it, he claims, were two floors of Udba that controlled the information going out. "These are God's wars, these are God's battles", he concludes.

sections.subtitle: Klin se klinom izbija: ustrajnost i kritika međureligijskih skupova
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar kritizira međureligijske susrete za mir
sections.content:
Unatoč tim plodovima, zlo je i dalje snažno prisutno, upozorava Grebenar, pa zajednica „nema drugog izbora“. **Klin se klinom izbija**: treba ostati zajedno u molitvi i postu. Izražava čvrsto uvjerenje da će Gospodin i nakon što ovaj podcast jednom završi održati na okupu zajednicu ljudi okupljenih oko molitve i posta, uvijek u jedinstvu sa „svetom majkom Crkvom“.

Na kraju se kratko osvrće na takozvani **„duh Asiza“**, međureligijske susrete na kojima predstavnici različitih religija, među njima i kršćani, zajedno govore o miru. Grebenar to naziva „igrokazom“ i smatra da od toga nema ništa. Opisuje to kao krivovjerje i „dijalog sa suvremenim svijetom“ koji **razara Crkvu iznutra**. Takvi skupovi, kaže, vjernicima poručuju da sve religije govore o dobru i da su sve od Boga. Tko tako postupa, tvrdi, nije branio Krista Gospodina i obezvrijedio je žrtvu na križu.

Naglašava da samo kršćani imaju Spasitelja, ali taj Spasitelj nije umro samo za njih, nego za cijeli svijet. Zato vjernici trebaju muslimanima, hinduistima, budistima i ateistima reći: **„Isus Krist umro je i za tebe.“**
sections.subtitle_en: Fighting fire with fire: perseverance and criticism of interreligious gatherings
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar criticizes interreligious meetings for peace
sections.content_en:
Despite these fruits, evil is still powerfully present, Grebenar warns, so the community "has no other choice". **One nail drives out another / like cures like**: one must remain together in prayer and fasting. He expresses a firm conviction that the Lord, even after this podcast one day ends, will keep together the community of people gathered around prayer and fasting, always in unity with "holy mother Church".

Finally, he briefly touches upon the so-called **“spirit of Assisi”**, interreligious meetings where representatives of different religions, among them Christians, speak together about peace. Grebenar calls this a "charade" and considers that nothing comes of it. He describes it as heresy and a "dialogue with the modern world" that **destroys the Church from within**. Such gatherings, he says, tell the faithful that all religions speak of the good and that all are from God. Whoever acts like that, he claims, has not defended Christ the Lord and has debased the sacrifice on the cross.

He emphasizes that only Christians have a Savior, but that Savior did not die only for them, but for the whole world. Therefore, believers should say to Muslims, Hindus, Buddhists, and atheists: **“Jesus Christ died for you too.”**

sections.subtitle: Ovce s desna, jarci s lijeva: evanđelje o posljednjem sudu
sections.screenshot_description: Vladimir Grebenar čita evanđelje o Sinu Čovječjem koji dolazi u slavi i razlučuje narode
sections.content:
Nakon dužeg tumačenja Izaijina proroštva o pokrivaču koji zastire sve narode, **Vladimir Grebenar**, voditelj podcasta Ora et Labora, čita evanđeoski odlomak dana. Riječ je o jednom od najdramatičnijih prizora u Svetom pismu, o slici posljednjeg suda.

Kad Sin Čovječji dođe u slavi i svi anđeli njegovi s njime, sjest će na prijestolje slave svoje. Pred njim će se sabrati svi narodi, a on će ih razlučiti kao što pastir razlučuje ovce od jaraca: ovce sebi s desna, jarce s lijeva. Onima s desna kralj će reći: „Dođite, blagoslovljeni Oca mojega! Primite u baštinu Kraljevstvo pripravljeno za vas od postanka svijeta.“

Obrazloženje presude jednostavno je i konkretno:
- bio je gladan i dali su mu jesti,
- bio je žedan i napojili su ga,
- bio je stranac i primili su ga,
- bio je gol i zaogrnuli su ga,
- bio je bolestan i pohodili su ga,
- bio je u tamnici i došli su k njemu.

Pravednici se čude i pitaju kada su ga to vidjeli u takvom stanju. Kralj im odgovara: „Zaista, kažem vam, što god učiniste jednom od ove moje najmanje braće, meni učiniste.“ Onima s lijeva reći će: „Odlazite od mene, prokleti, u oganj vječni, pripravljen đavlu i anđelima njegovim.“ Oni su propustili činiti upravo ta djela. Odlomak završava rečenicom koja će obilježiti cijelo tumačenje: „I otići će ovi u muku vječnu, a pravednici u život vječni.“
sections.subtitle_en: Sheep on the right, goats on the left: the Gospel of the Last Judgment
sections.screenshot_description_en: Vladimir Grebenar reads the Gospel of the Son of Man coming in glory and separating the nations
sections.content_en:
After a lengthy interpretation of Isaiah's prophecy about the veil that covers all peoples, **Vladimir Grebenar**, host of the podcast Ora et Labora, reads the Gospel passage of the day. It is one of the most dramatic scenes in Sacred Scripture, the image of the Last Judgment.

When the Son of Man comes in His glory, and all the angels with Him, He will sit on the throne of His glory. All the nations will be gathered before Him, and He will separate them as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats: the sheep on His right, the goats on the left. To those on the right, the King will say: "Come, you who are blessed by my Father! Inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world."

The reasoning of the judgment is simple and concrete:
- He was hungry and they gave Him to eat,
- He was thirsty and they gave Him drink,
- He was a stranger and they welcomed Him,
- He was naked and they clothed Him,
- He was sick and they visited Him,
- He was in prison and they came to Him.

The righteous are amazed and ask when they saw Him in such a state. The King replies to them: "Truly, I say to you, whatever you did for one of these least brothers of mine, you did for me." To those on the left He will say: "Depart from me, you accursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels." They failed to do precisely those deeds. The passage ends with the sentence that will characterize the entire interpretation: "And these will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life."

sections.subtitle: Sud nakon uskrsnuća: razdvajanje će proći i kroz hrvatski narod
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj objašnjava da će na posljednjem sudu i hrvatski narod biti podijeljen na ovce i jarce
sections.content:
Vladimir Grebenar pojašnjava da evanđelje opisuje **posljednji sud**, koji dolazi nakon općeg uskrsnuća. Tada će svi ljudi uskrsnuti i svi narodi stajat će pred Isusom.

Voditelj zatim sliku primjenjuje na vlastiti narod. Poziva slušatelje da zamisle kako će i unutar hrvatskog naroda jedan dio biti odvojen među ovce, a drugi među jarce. Koliki će udio biti s koje strane, ističe, nitko ne zna.

Kao primjer navodi mogućnost da se spasi samo pet posto ljudi. U tom scenariju on sam može završiti na strani jaraca, a netko od slušatelja na strani ovaca. Takav ishod naziva tragedijom: tada je sve gotovo i, kako slikovito kaže, „nema mogućnosti za popravni“. Knjige života su napisane i sve je već rečeno i učinjeno. Čovjek tada Isusu može govoriti bilo što, ali On ga više ne želi slušati.

Grebenar podsjeća da Sveto pismo taj dan naziva **velikim i strašnim danom**.
sections.subtitle_en: Judgment after the resurrection: the separation will pass through the Croatian people as well
sections.screenshot_description_en: Host explains that at the Last Judgment the Croatian people will also be divided into sheep and goats
sections.content_en:
Vladimir Grebenar explains that the Gospel describes the **Last Judgment**, which comes after the general resurrection. Then all people will rise and all nations will stand before Jesus.

The host then applies the image to his own nation. He invites listeners to imagine how within the Croatian people as well one part will be separated among the sheep, and the other among the goats. What proportion will be on which side, he points out, no one knows.

As an example, he mentions the possibility that only five percent of people are saved. In that scenario, he himself could end up on the side of the goats, and one of the listeners on the side of the sheep. He calls such an outcome a tragedy: then everything is finished and, as he puts it graphically, "there is no chance for a retake". The books of life are written and everything has already been said and done. A person may say anything to Jesus then, but He no longer wants to listen.

Grebenar recalls that Sacred Scripture calls that day a **great and terrible day**.

sections.subtitle: Znoj za volanom: osobno razmatranje o danu suda
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar priča kako mu se tresu noge i kako se preznojavao u automobilu razmišljajući o sudu
sections.content:
Vladimir Grebenar u ovom dijelu otvoreno govori o vlastitom doživljaju. Kad pomisli na dan suda, priznaje, noge mu se tresu.

Opisuje nedavni događaj. Vraćao se automobilom s jednog skupa i u autu molio krunicu. Nakon molitve došla mu je misao da razmišlja o posljednjem sudu i da Gospodin želi da o tome govori. Zamislio je sebe u toj situaciji: uskrsnuo je, ide na sud i ne zna na koju će stranu biti postavljen. Počeo se, kaže, preznojavati za volanom.

Grebenar naglašava kako je riječ o neizvjesnosti u kojoj je **cijela vječnost u pitanju**. U vrlo slikovitim kontrastima opisuje dvije mogućnosti:

- **Raj**: ono što „oko nije vidjelo, uho nije čulo“. Vječni život, vječna radost i vječno jedinstvo u ljubavi. Nema bolesti, kriza ni nesreća. Uvijek je dan, a Kristova svjetlost neprestano obasjava sve.
- **Pakao**: stanje nalik zatvorenosti u mrtvačkoj škrinji iz koje se ne može izaći. Čovjek je svjestan svega, sve oko njega trune i zaudara, a bol stalno raste, cijelu vječnost.

Zaključuje da je to izbor, i ponavlja: „To je izbor.“
sections.subtitle_en: Sweat behind the wheel: personal reflection on the day of judgment
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar tells how his legs shake and how he was breaking into a sweat in the car thinking about the judgment
sections.content_en:
In this part, Vladimir Grebenar speaks openly about his own experience. When he thinks of the day of judgment, he admits, his legs shake.

He describes a recent event. He was returning by car from a gathering and praying the Rosary in the car. After the prayer, a thought came to him to think about the final judgment and that the Lord wants him to speak about it. He imagined himself in that situation: he has resurrected, he is going to judgment, and he does not know which side he will be placed on. He began, he says, to break into a sweat behind the wheel.

Grebenar emphasizes that it is about an uncertainty in which **the whole eternity is at stake**. In very vivid contrasts, he describes two possibilities:

- **Heaven**: that which "eye has not seen, ear has not heard." Eternal life, eternal joy, and eternal unity in love. There is no illness, crises, or misfortunes. It is always day, and the light of Christ constantly shines upon everything.
- **Hell**: a state akin to being enclosed in a coffin from which one cannot get out. A person is aware of everything, everything around him rots and stinks, and the pain constantly grows, for all eternity.

He concludes that it is a choice, and repeats: "It is a choice."

sections.subtitle: Sve kroz prizmu spasenja: nije dovoljno govoriti „Gospodine, Gospodine“
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj poziva slušatelje da se pokrenu i čine djela, a ne samo mole i poste
sections.content:
Iz takvog razmatranja, objašnjava Grebenar, proizlazi vrlo praktičan zaključak. Treba paziti što se govori jer će se odgovarati za svaku riječ. Još je važnije, kaže, paziti **što se sluša i čita**. Cijeli život trebalo bi prilagoditi jednom cilju, spasenju. Sve što čovjek radi trebalo bi promatrati kroz prizmu spasenja, a ne raditi tek „reda radi“.

To pitanje voditelj postavlja i sebi: je li podcast koji snima na spasenje njemu i slušateljima? Odgovara da mora biti poticajan.

Zatim ističe da je Isus Krist Gospodin, Sin Božji i jedini koji je umro na križu i dao život za spasenje ljudi. Iz toga izvodi poziv: **„Pokrenimo se!“** Nije dovoljno samo moliti i postiti. Treba činiti djela, kako bi u knjizi života bilo zapisano nešto učinjeno za Gospodina. Tko se sav zauzme za Isusa, kaže, zauzima se i za vlastito spasenje i za spasenje drugih te svjedoči za Gospodina.

Vraćajući se evanđelju, Grebenar upozorava na jedan detalj. I oni na lijevoj strani Isusa oslovljavaju s „Gospodine“, dakle i oni su bili vjernici koji su ga priznavali. Zato, podsjeća, Isus kaže da neće svaki koji govori „Gospodine, Gospodine“ ući u Kraljevstvo nebesko, nego onaj koji vrši volju Oca. Spašavaju se oni koji su „u pokretu“, koji čine.
sections.subtitle_en: Everything through the prism of salvation: it is not enough to say „Lord, Lord“
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host invites listeners to get moving and do deeds, not just pray and fast
sections.content_en:
From such reflection, Grebenar explains, comes a very practical conclusion. One must be careful what one says because one will answer for every word. It is even more important, he says, to be careful **what one listens to and reads**. One's whole life should be adapted to a single goal, salvation. Everything a person does should be viewed through the prism of salvation, and not done merely "for the sake of order."

The host also poses this question to himself: is the podcast he is recording for his salvation and that of his listeners? He answers that it must be encouraging.

Then he points out that Jesus Christ is Lord, the Son of God, and the only one who died on the cross and gave his life for the salvation of people. From this he derives a call: **"Let us get moving!"** It is not enough merely to pray and fast. One must do deeds, so that something done for the Lord is written in the book of life. Whoever commits entirely to Jesus, he says, commits to both his own salvation and the salvation of others and witnesses for the Lord.

Returning to the Gospel, Grebenar warns of one detail. Even those on the left side address Jesus as "Lord," meaning they too were believers who acknowledged him. That is why, he recalls, Jesus says that not everyone who says "Lord, Lord" will enter the Kingdom of heaven, but the one who does the will of the Father. Those who are "in motion," who act, are saved.

sections.subtitle: Zlatno pravilo protiv pasivnosti i oštra kritika međureligijskih susreta
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar uspoređuje kršćansko zlatno pravilo s kineskom filozofijom
sections.content:
Grebenar dalje izlaže ono što naziva **zlatnim pravilom spasenja**: „Čini drugome što želiš da drugi tebi čini.“ Tome suprotstavlja „ljudsku mudrost“ kineske filozofije, koja kaže: „Ne čini drugome što ne želiš da drugi tebi čini.“ Takav pristup, smatra, vodi u propast jer čovjeka čini pasivnim i sklonim tome da se nikome ne zamjeri.

U istu kategoriju svrstava međureligijske susrete na kojima predstavnici raznih religija i kršćani zajedno govore o miru. Takve inicijative naziva **izdajom Isusa Krista** jer, prema njegovu tumačenju, prešućuju da je Isus Sin Božji koji je umro na križu. Da bi se s pripadnikom druge religije moglo razgovarati o miru ili s njim postiti, kaže voditelj, najprije mu treba reći da je Isus Krist Sin Božji, umro na križu za sve ljude.

Kao uporište navodi Isusov nalog: „Idite po svem svijetu, propovijedajte evanđelje.“ Tko povjeruje i pokrsti se, spasit će se, a tko ne povjeruje, bit će osuđen jer nije povjerovao u jedinorođenoga Sina Božjega. „Točka. Nema dalje“, poručuje Grebenar. To je za njega kriterij svakog razgovora.

Precizira ipak da dijalog s nekršćanima o **svjetovnim pitanjima** smatra prihvatljivim. Kao primjere navodi poduzetništvo te izradu zakona, akata i uredbi. Kad je riječ o pitanjima vjere, svi se moraju prilagoditi jer je pisano: „Svaki će jezik priznati: Isus Krist jest Gospodin, na slavu Boga Oca.“ To prema njegovu tumačenju ne znači da će svaki čovjek to priznati, nego da će u svakom narodu barem jedna osoba izgovoriti to ispovijedanje.
sections.subtitle_en: The Golden Rule against passivity and sharp criticism of interreligious meetings
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar compares the Christian Golden Rule with Chinese philosophy
sections.content_en:
Grebenar further expounds what he calls the **Golden Rule of salvation**: "Do to another what you want another to do to you." To this he contrasts the "human wisdom" of Chinese philosophy, which says: "Do not do to another what you do not want another to do to you." Such an approach, he believes, leads to ruin because it makes a person passive and prone to not offending anyone.

Into the same category he places interreligious meetings where representatives of various religions and Christians speak together about peace. He calls such initiatives a **betrayal of Jesus Christ** because, according to his interpretation, they keep silent about Jesus being the Son of God who died on the cross. In order to be able to speak about peace with a member of another religion or fast with him, says the host, one must first tell him that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, who died on the cross for all people.

As a foundation he cites Jesus's mandate: "Go into all the world, proclaim the Gospel." Whoever believes and is baptized will be saved, but whoever does not believe will be condemned because he did not believe in the only-begotten Son of God. "Period. Nothing beyond that," says Grebenar. That is for him the criterion of every conversation.

He specifies, however, that he considers dialogue with non-Christians on **secular matters** acceptable. As examples, he cites entrepreneurship and the drafting of laws, acts, and regulations. When it comes to matters of faith, everyone must conform because it is written: "Every tongue will confess: Jesus Christ is Lord, to the glory of God the Father." According to his interpretation, this does not mean that every person will confess it, but that in every nation at least one person will utter that confession.

sections.subtitle: Hereze „gore od Arijeve“
sections.screenshot_description: Grebenar govori o suvremenim herezama i uspoređuje ih s arijanizmom
sections.content:
Takav govor, objašnjava Grebenar, potreban je kako bi se spriječilo da se u narodu i Crkvi rađaju hereze. Ako se ne tvrdi da je Isus Krist Sin Božji i da nema spasenja osim po njemu, takvo je naviještanje evanđelja po njegovu sudu heretično, i to **gore od Arijeva**.

Podsjeća na Arija iz ranog kršćanstva, koji je naučavao da Isus nije od vječnosti, nego da ga je Bog stvorio kao stvorenje. Zbog toga je bio izopćen iz Crkve. Današnje pojave voditelj opisuje kao „hereze na entu potenciju“.

Zaključuje da kršćani danas trebaju **braniti Isusa Krista**, jer se tako brani i Crkva. Kritizira to što je, kako kaže, postalo važnije pojavljivati se na društvenim mrežama i u medijima, tumačiti hereze i pozivati narod na njih nego braniti Krista.
sections.subtitle_en: Heresies „worse than Arius's“
sections.screenshot_description_en: Grebenar speaks about contemporary heresies and compares them with Arianism
sections.content_en:
Such discourse, Grebenar explains, is necessary in order to prevent heresies from being born among the people and in the Church. If it is not asserted that Jesus Christ is the Son of God and that there is no salvation except through him, such proclamation of the Gospel is, in his judgment, heretical, and that **worse than Arius's**.

He recalls Arius from early Christianity, who taught that Jesus is not from eternity, but that God created him as a creature. Because of that, he was excommunicated from the Church. The host describes today's occurrences as "heresies to the nth power."

He concludes that Christians today need to **defend Jesus Christ**, because in that way the Church is defended as well. He criticizes the fact that, as he says, it has become more important to appear on social networks and in the media, interpreting heresies and calling the people to them, than to defend Christ.

sections.subtitle: Strah Božji u kostima i samo dvoja vrata vječnosti
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj priznaje da se boji za vlastito spasenje
sections.content:
U jednom od najosobnijih trenutaka emisije Vladimir Grebenar navodi riječi psalma: „Blago onome tko se boji Gospodina.“ Priznaje da se boji Gospodina i posljednjeg suda, toliko da mu je, kako kaže, strah Božji „u kostima“. Na tom daru zahvaljuje Bogu. Upravo mu taj strah, objašnjava, daje snagu da mu nije teško snimati, putovati, raditi i pozivati ljude na obraćenje.

Iskreno dodaje da se boji da se neće spasiti. Poziva se na svetog Pavla, koji je pisao da ne misli da je to već postigao. Ako tako govori apostol, pita se voditelj, što onda reći za sebe, kojega naziva „crvom običnim, nitko i ništa“. Čvrsto vjeruje da je ispravan pristup vjeri bojati se Boga i dobro paziti kako se svjedoči za Isusa.

Za kraj tumačenja vraća se zaključnoj rečenici evanđelja. Jedni odlaze u muku vječnu, odnosno u smrt i pakao, a pravednici koji su vršili volju Božju u život vječni. Na kraju postoje **samo dvoja vrata**. Čak će se i čistilište jednog dana zatvoriti, kad iz njega izađe posljednja duša. Kad prođe vrijeme, ostaju samo dvije stvarnosti: pakao, odnosno muka vječna, i život vječni.

Tumačenje završava porukom: „Pazimo dobro sada već na kojoj smo strani.“
sections.subtitle_en: Fear of God in the bones and only two gates of eternity
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host admits that he fears for his own salvation
sections.content_en:
In one of the most personal moments of the show, Vladimir Grebenar quotes the words of the psalm: "Blessed is the one who fears the Lord." He admits that he fears the Lord and the final judgment, so much that, as he says, the fear of God is "in his bones." He thanks God for that gift. Precisely that fear, he explains, gives him strength so that it is not hard for him to record, travel, work, and call people to conversion.

He honestly adds that he fears he will not be saved. He refers to Saint Paul, who wrote that he does not think he has already attained it. If an apostle speaks that way, the host asks, what then to say for himself, whom he calls "an ordinary worm, a nobody and nothing." He firmly believes that the correct approach to faith is to fear God and pay close attention to how one witnesses for Jesus.

To conclude the interpretation, he returns to the concluding sentence of the Gospel. Some go into eternal punishment, that is, into death and hell, and the righteous who did the will of God into eternal life. In the end, there are **only two doors**. Even purgatory will one day be closed, when the last soul exits it. When time passes, only two realities remain: hell, that is, eternal punishment, and eternal life.

The interpretation ends with the message: "Let us pay close attention already now to which side we are on."
